## Solution

**Setup.** Label the dwarfs by their heights $1 < 2 < 3 < 4 < 5 < 6 < 7$. An ordering is a permutation $\pi$ of $\{1,\dots,7\}$. For each adjacent pair define the sign
$$s_i = \begin{cases} + & \text{if } \pi_i < \pi_{i+1},\\ - & \text{if } \pi_i > \pi_{i+1}, \end{cases}\qquad i=1,\dots,6.$$
Since all heights are distinct, every $s_i$ is well defined.

**Key observation.** Three successive dwarfs $\pi_i,\pi_{i+1},\pi_{i+2}$ are increasing exactly when $s_i=s_{i+1}=+$, and decreasing exactly when $s_i=s_{i+1}=-$. The condition "no three successive dwarfs are increasing or decreasing" therefore forbids both $++$ and $--$ as consecutive pairs in the sign sequence. Hence **every two consecutive signs must differ**, so the sign sequence is forced to alternate:
$$\text{either } +-+-+-+ \text{ or } -+-+-+.$$

Thus a valid ordering is exactly an **alternating (zigzag) permutation** — either up-down-up-down-up-down ($\pi_1<\pi_2>\pi_3<\pi_4>\pi_5<\pi_6>\pi_7$) or down-up-down-up-down-up-down ($\pi_1>\pi_2<\pi_3>\pi_4<\pi_5>\pi_6<\pi_7$).

**Counting.** The number of up-down permutations of $\{1,\dots,n\}$ is the Euler zigzag number $E_n$, with exponential generating function
$$\sum_{n\ge 0} E_n\frac{x^n}{n!} = \sec x + \tan x.$$
Expanding:
$$\sec x = 1 + \tfrac{x^2}{2} + \tfrac{5x^4}{24} + \tfrac{61x^6}{720}+\cdots,\qquad \tan x = x + \tfrac{2x^3}{6} + \tfrac{16x^5}{120} + \tfrac{272x^7}{5040}+\cdots,$$
so reading off coefficients:
$$E_0=1,\; E_1=1,\; E_2=1,\; E_3=2,\; E_4=5,\; E_5=16,\; E_6=61,\; \boxed{E_7=272}.$$

By symmetry (replacing each height $h$ by $8-h$ swaps up-down and down-up permutations), the number of down-up permutations of 7 elements also equals $E_7 = 272$.

**Sanity check.** For $n=3$: valid orderings of $\{1,2,3\}$ are all permutations except $123$ and $321$, giving $4 = 2E_3 = 2\cdot 2$. ✓  
For $n=4$: the up-down-up permutations are $1324,1423,2314,2413,3412$, exactly $5=E_4$, and doubling gives $10$. ✓

**Final count.** The two alternating patterns are disjoint (the first sign differs), so the total number of valid orders is
$$E_7 + E_7 = 2\cdot 272 = \boxed{544}.$$
